subject: Model shortlist & token-profile runbook for production onboarding

Subject: Model shortlist & token-profile runbook for production onboarding

Hi Tara —

Following our kickoff yesterday I wanted to share a concise runbook that stitches together the model shortlist, context-length guidance, and token-volume estimates for AcquiHealth's initial LLM use case (patient intake summarization + claim tagging). Attached are: onboarding-runbook.xlsx (MAL & IT milestones), sample-token-profiles.csv (token estimates by endpoint), and a draft mutual action plan.

High-level recommendation (short):
- Model shortlist: rdm-gt-11b-q4f (16k context), rdm-6b-8k-quant (8k context), and rdm-2.7b-fast (4k context) as a fallback for latency-sensitive paths.
- Context guidance: canonical patient note + recent encounter + structured meta (up to 6k tokens typical). We recommend enabling prefix/KV caching on repeated patient context to reduce cost for re-reads.
- Token volumes: projected avg prompt tokens = 2.2k, avg completion tokens = 180; peak concurrent requests ~45 qps for phase-1. See sample-token-profiles.csv for per-route breakdown.

Open questions we flagged for you:
1) Will the engineering team do server-side chunking of very long notes (>=20k tokens) or should we provide streaming chunk assembly on our side?
2) Any constraints on storing KV cache or are all patient contexts required to be ephemeral (no persistence)?

Next steps we suggest this week:
- Confirm chunking approach (you or Eng Team)
- Pick primary model for Phase-1 (we can default to rdm-6b-8k-quant if you want cost parity)
- Kick off a two-week model sprint (we'll provide test prompts and eval harness)

I'll be available for a 30-min sync after 1pm PT today if that's convenient.

Thanks,

--
Dylan Brooks
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: onboarding-runbook.xlsx (spreadsheet), sample-token-profiles.csv (csv), rdw-mutual-action-plan.docx (docx)

Thanks, Dylan — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from Eng:

- For very long historical notes, we plan to do server-side chunking for initial MVP (we chunk at sentence boundaries and include timestamp metadata). Can you confirm how prefix/KV caching would interact with server-side chunking? If chunks are assembled client-side, will Redwood still get the benefit of KV cache?
- Regarding persistence: compliance wants ephemeral by default but we can allow short-term (24–72h) cache retention if that helps latency. What are the tradeoffs?

Also, cost-wise: can you give a rough monthly estimate assuming 3M tokens in prompts and 250k tokens in outputs? That will help our procurement team.

Tara
Tara Singh
Head of Product, AcquiHealth

Subject: Re: Model shortlist & token-profile runbook for production onboarding

Tara — thanks for the quick questions, and great to hear Eng will handle chunking for the MVP. Short answers below, followed by cost ballpark and a recommended path.

- KV/prefix caching + server-side chunking:
  * If Eng sends discrete chunk requests (each chunk as its own prompt) KV caching will still help for repeated chunks (for example, boilerplate header/meta). However, cross-chunk attention benefits only apply if you send the concatenated context in one call to a long-context model (16k).
  * Recommended: use server-side chunking for ingestion + keep a short-lived (24–48h) KV cache for the most-recently-accessed patient to cover multi-turn flows; this gives most latency wins while satisfying your ephemeral requirement.

- Tradeoffs for short-term cache retention:
  * 24–72h cache improves response time for multi-step workflows and cuts token spend on repeated context by up to ~30–40% depending on access patterns.
  * Compliance impact: short retention window reduces surface area and still supports auditability if you keep cache metadata (not raw contents). We can add optional encryption-at-rest and audit hooks.

- Rough monthly cost (ballpark):
  * Assumptions: 3,000,000 prompt tokens/month + 250,000 completion tokens/month; baseline model rdm-6b-8k-quant at $0.0009 per prompt-token equivalent, $0.0015 per completion-token equivalent (example blended pricing for dedicated tier).
  * Estimated: prompt cost ~ $2,700; completion cost ~ $375; subtotal ~ $3,075/mo. With caching (30% saving on prompts) expected net ~ $2,150/mo. Note this excludes Dedicated commit fees or reserved capacity pricing — I can re-run with Dedicated assumptions if you want.

- Model choice recommendation: Start with rdm-6b-8k-quant as primary for Phase-1, enable rdm-gt-11b-q4f only for long-document processor endpoint (batch/async) where higher context is required. Use rdm-2.7b-fast as fallback for UI paths needing <150ms p95.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Confirm cache retention policy (24h vs 72h) — we'll prepare the config.
2) If procurement wants an explicit pricing line item we'll convert the above to a simple SOW estimate.
3) Schedule a 30-min model-sprint planning session next Tue to lock the shortlist and test prompts.

I'll attach a small diagram and the price calc in a follow-up.

—D
